correctness.rationale: The derivative supremum reduces exactly to the initial-velocity functional by contraction of right shifts. For the conjugate pair, phase reduction gives an exhaustive single-variable expression whose denominator switches once because exp(r u)(cos u-r sin u) has negative derivative on (0,pi). The two branches are respectively strictly unimodal and strictly decreasing, giving the unique globally optimal contact phase. An explicitly normalized extremizer attains the bound; strict monotonicity of the scalar threshold function gives the unique parameter boundary. Implicit differentiation yields a continuous first derivative and a strictly negative second-derivative jump. The strong-damping asymptotic follows from convergence of the unique bounded scaled root. The same constant for complex-valued inputs follows by translation, phase rotation and real-part reduction. A standard-library checker passed 174116 supplementary phase/trajectory comparisons and direct coefficient searches; these tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The exact maximal initial velocity of a uniformly bounded, underdamped second-order linear oscillator is a natural two-dimensional nonreal spectral benchmark singled out by the general exponential-polynomial inequality problem. The sharp coefficient shows a genuine contact-geometry transition at a uniquely specified physical damping ratio; it is C1 but not C2 there, has explicit extremizers, and matches the known repeated-real-root asymptotic coefficient as frequency vanishes. These facts answer a motivated structural and exact-constant gap, not an arbitrary numerical slice or an unmotivated parameter substitution.
